column1: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.
column3: Who has stood by you through a hard season of life?
column4: What did they do that you still remember today?

column1: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
column3: When has a gentle reply calmed a tense moment you were part of?
column4: What helps you stay soft when someone comes at you hard?

column1: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
column3: Who is the friend who sharpens you most?
column4: How have they changed the way you think or work?

column1: Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
column3: What kind word lifted you when you were weighed down by worry?
column4: Who could use that same kind word from you this week?

column1: A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
column3: What reliably makes you laugh until you feel better?
column4: When has cheerfulness carried you through something tough?

column1: A glad heart makes a cheerful face, but an aching heart breaks the spirit.
column3: Whose face always seems to light up when they see you?
column4: What would it take for you to be that person for someone else?

column1: A man of many companions may be ruined, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
column3: Which friend has felt closer to you than family?
column4: How did that friendship grow so deep?

column1: Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster. A neighbor who is near is better than a distant brother.
column3: Which neighbor or nearby friend has shown up for you when it mattered?
column4: What makes a good neighbor in your eyes?

column1: Where there is no counsel, plans fail; but in a multitude of counselors they are established.
column3: What plan of yours turned out better because you asked others for input?
column4: Whose advice do you seek first when making a big decision and why?

column1: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who is wise listens to counsel.
column3: When did listening to someone's advice save you from a mistake?
column4: What makes it hard for you to take advice sometimes?

column1: He who answers before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
column3: When did you jump to an answer before hearing the whole story?
column4: What helps you slow down and listen fully?

column1: He who pleads his cause first seems right— until another comes and questions him.
column3: When did hearing the other side of a story completely change your mind?
column4: How do you make sure you hear both sides before you judge?

column1: The discretion of a man makes him slow to anger. It is his glory to overlook an offense.
column3: What is an offense you chose to overlook that you are glad you let go?
column4: What makes some hurts easier to let go of than others?

column1: One who is slow to anger is better than the mighty; one who rules his spirit, than he who takes a city.
column3: What is a moment when keeping your cool took more strength than losing it?
column4: What helps you rule your own spirit when you feel provoked?

column1: Joy comes to a man with the reply of his mouth. How good is a word at the right time!
column3: What is the best thing anyone ever said to you at exactly the right time?
column4: How did those words change what happened next?

column1: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
column3: What compliment or encouragement has stayed with you for years?
column4: Why do you think those words landed so well?

column1: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
column3: Whose words always seem to leave you feeling better?
column4: What do they say or do that makes their words so sweet?

column1: There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.
column3: When have someone's words helped heal a hurt in you?
column4: How do you try to use your own words to heal?

column1: Even a fool, when he keeps silent, is counted wise. When he shuts his lips, he is thought to be discerning.
column3: When were you glad you kept quiet instead of speaking up?
column4: How do you decide when to speak and when to stay silent?

column1: Whoever guards his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from troubles.
column3: What trouble have you avoided simply by holding your tongue?
column4: What is your best trick for pausing before you speak?

column1: In all hard work there is profit, but the talk of the lips leads only to poverty.
column3: What hard work in your life has paid off most?
column4: What kept you going when the work felt endless?

column1: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He won’t serve obscure men.
column3: What skill have you worked hardest to master?
column4: Who helped you most along the way?

column1: A man’s heart plans his course, but Yahweh directs his steps.
column3: When did life lead you somewhere very different from what you had planned?
column4: What did that detour teach you?

column1: The plans of the diligent surely lead to profit; and everyone who is hasty surely rushes to poverty.
column3: What is something you achieved through careful steady planning?
column4: What part of planning comes naturally to you and what part is a struggle?

column1: Prepare your work outside, and get your fields ready. Afterwards, build your house.
column3: What foundation did you lay early in life that you are thankful for now?
column4: What groundwork are you laying today for your future?

column1: Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.
column3: What surprise has a single day brought you that changed everything?
column4: How has that experience shaped the way you think about tomorrow?

column1: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled, it is a tree of life.
column3: What longing in your life was finally fulfilled after a long wait?
column4: How did you keep hope alive while you waited?

column1: One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
column3: Who are the wise people whose company has made you wiser?
column4: What is one thing you picked up just from being around them?

column1: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.
column3: When did someone else's praise of you mean more than anything you could say about yourself?
column4: Why do you think praise from others feels so different?

column1: When pride comes, then comes shame, but with humility comes wisdom.
column3: When did a bit of humility open the door to learning something new?
column4: What helps you stay humble when things are going well?

column1: Pride goes before destruction, and an arrogant spirit before a fall.
column3: What is a time your own pride tripped you up?
column4: What did you learn from that fall?

column1: A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.
column3: What do you hope people say about you when you are not in the room?
column4: What are you doing now to earn that kind of name?

column1: Better is a dinner of herbs, where love is, than a fattened calf with hatred.
column3: What simple meal shared with people you love stands out in your memory?
column4: What made that time around the table so special?

column1: Better is a dry morsel with quietness, than a house full of feasting with strife.
column3: Where do you find the most peace and quiet in your life?
column4: What would you give up to have more of it?

column1: Don’t withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it.
column3: When did someone do you a good turn simply because it was in their power?
column4: What good is in your power to do for someone right now?

column1: He who has a generous eye will be blessed, for he shares his food with the poor.
column3: Who is the most generous person you have ever known?
column4: What did their generosity teach you about sharing?

column1: The merciful man does good to his own soul, but he who is cruel troubles his own flesh.
column3: When has showing mercy to someone ended up doing you good as well?
column4: What makes mercy easier or harder for you to give?

column1: Children’s children are the crown of old men; the glory of children is their parents.
column3: What do you treasure most about the generations in your family?
column4: What family story do you hope gets passed down?

column1: The glory of young men is their strength. The splendor of old men is their gray hair.
column3: What strengths of youth and wisdom of age have you seen come together well?
column4: What do you most want to learn from those older than you?

column1: Like cold water to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
column3: What good news from far away has refreshed you like cold water?
column4: Who far away would love to hear good news from you?

column1: Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man.
column3: What does your heart reveal about you that people might not see at first?
column4: How has your inner life shaped who you have become?

column1: The wounds of a friend are faithful, although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
column3: When did a friend tell you a hard truth that you needed to hear?
column4: How did that honesty change your friendship?

column1: Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart; so does earnest counsel from a man’s friend.
column3: What earnest advice from a friend brought you joy?
column4: How do you know when a friend's counsel comes from the heart?

column1: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
column3: What do you do to guard your heart and keep it healthy?
column4: What drains your heart and what fills it back up?

column1: An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.
column3: Who is the most honest person you know?
column4: What does their honesty give you that flattery never could?

column1: Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out.
column3: Who has drawn out the deep thoughts in your heart?
column4: What questions do they ask that help you open up?

column1: He who covers an offense promotes love; but he who repeats a matter separates best friends.
column3: When has letting a past wrong go helped a relationship grow stronger?
column4: What does forgiving without retelling the story look like for you?

column1: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.
column3: Where have you seen love cover a wrong and bring people back together?
column4: What makes love strong enough to cover things?

column1: Don’t let kindness and truth forsake you. Bind them around your neck. Write them on the tablet of your heart.
column3: Who in your life best combines kindness and truth?
column4: How do you hold on to both when they seem to pull apart?

column1: The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.
column3: What brings your heart the deepest sense of peace?
column4: How do you handle envy when it creeps in?

column1: For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.
column3: When have you seen a quarrel die down because no one kept it going?
column4: What helps you stop feeding gossip or conflict?

column1: One who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but one who is of a trustworthy spirit is one who keeps a secret.
column3: Who do you trust to keep your secrets safe?
column4: What makes someone trustworthy in your eyes?
